text:
Marathon Petroleum gained 2.8% today, climbing to $471.68, as oil prices stabilized after several days of geopolitical anxiety. The stock has surged 20% over two weeks alongside crude—U.S. oil is trading at $96 per barrel today while Brent (global crude) sits around $106, both elevated by conflict risks in the Middle East and uncertainty over Russian sanctions. Refineries are running at 92.7% capacity, a healthy level that means the company can convert higher crude costs into refined products like diesel and gasoline at decent margins.

The near-term narrative has shifted from pure crisis to cautious calculation: Trump's reported diesel deal with Russia would add supplies but represents less than two weeks of U.S. demand, so it won't crater prices overnight. Meanwhile, the Saudi-Houthi conflict and Iran nuclear tensions remain live risks that could disrupt supplies again, keeping a floor under crude valuations and supporting refinery profitability. For a refiner like this, that combination of decent utilization rates and crude prices elevated by supply anxiety—rather than demand strength—tends to sustain margins without the downside risk of demand collapse.
